title: Human TCR alpha and beta RNA-based RACE protocol with unique molecular barcoding
protocol: Perform isolation of mononuclear cells from whole blood using Ficoll Paque density gradient centrifugation.
Optionally purify T cell subset of interest using magnetic separation or fluorescence-activated cell sorting.
Directly sort purified limited number of cells into RLT buffer for lysis and RNA protection.
Use column-based RNA isolation method, for example, RNeasy Micro kit (QIAGEN).
Culture thawed cells overnight in RPMI-1640 supplemented with 10% human serum if using frozen samples.
Verify RNA quantity and quality, e.g., using Agilent Bioanalyzer or gel electrophoresis.
Store cellular lysate in RLT buffer at -70°C for up to a month.
Store RNA in 75% ethanol at least one year at -20°C or at least one week at 4°C.
Start cDNA synthesis immediately after RNA extraction if less than 100 ng of RNA is available.
Mix the following reagents in a final volume of 20 μl in a sterile thin-walled 0.2 ml reaction tube:
- First Strand Buffer (5x, Clontech): 4 μl
- DTT (20 mM): 2 μl
- dNTP solution (10 mM each): 2 μl
- cDNA synthesis primer mix* (10 μM each): ACR_st4 & BCR4short: 2 μl
- 5’-template switch adapter (10 μM): 2 μl
- SMARTScribe Reverse Transcriptase (10x, Clontech): 2 μl
- rRNasin (Promega): 1 µl
- RNA: 1-5 µl
- mQ: 0-4 µl
Place the reaction tube(s) into a thermal cycler and incubate for 60 minutes at 42°C.
Add 1 μl of Uracyl DNA glycosylase (5 U/μl, New England Biolabs).
Incubate for 40 min at 37°C.
Purify cDNA using MinElute PCR Purification Kit (Qiagen).
Wash twice with PE buffer during purification.
Elute with 14 µl EB buffer.
Carry out first PCR amplification with Q5 polymerase (NEB, M0491L, 500 units) for 21 cycles.
Mix 1st strand cDNA with Q5 polymerase buffer in a final volume of 50 μl.
Add dNTP mix to the reaction mixture.
Pipette M1ss primer into the reaction tube.
Add reverse primers mix (ACR_st1 & BC2uniR) to the reaction.
Incubate the reaction with Q5 polymerase.
Add nuclease-free water to adjust the volume to 50 μl.
Perform PCR denaturation at 98°C for 10 seconds.
Anneal the PCR product at 55°C for 10 seconds.
Extend the PCR product at 72°C for 50 seconds.
Repeat cycles of denaturing, annealing, and extending for a total of 21 cycles.
Combine PCR products obtained from the same RNA sample.
Purify the combined PCR products using the QIAquick PCR purification kit.
Wash the purified PCR products twice during purification.
Elute the purified PCR product in 30 μl elution buffer.
Store purified product from the 1st PCR at 4°C overnight for short-term storage.
For extended storage (1-2 months), store the purified 1st PCR product at -20°C.
Mix purified 1st PCR product in a sterile thin-walled 0.2 ml reaction tube.
Add 10 μl of Q5 polymerase buffer to the reaction tube.
Pipette 1 μl of dNTP mix (10 mM each) into the reaction mixture.
Add 1 μl of M1s primer with sample barcode (10 µM).
Add 1 μl of hum bcj_i/hum acj_i primer with sample barcode (10 µM).
Pipette 0.5 μl of Q5 polymerase into the tube.
Add nuclease-free water to achieve a final volume of 50 μl, adjusting between 34.5-35.5 μl as necessary.
In some cases, dilute the 1st PCR product before mixing with other reagents to enhance efficiency of the 2nd PCR.
Mix M1s primers with different numbers of random nucleotides at the 5’-end for different samples (2, 3, or 4 nt).
Perform PCR using denature conditions at 98°C for 10 seconds.
Perform PCR using anneal conditions at 58°C for 10 seconds.
Perform PCR using extend conditions at 72°C for 50 seconds.
Repeat PCR cycles 10-16 times.
Analyze an aliquot of the sample alongside DNA ladder on agarose gel or Agilent Bioanalyzer.
Verify quality and concentration of obtained PCR product.
Observe a visible band (~2 ng/ul) within 9-15 cycles of second PCR.
Purify PCR product using QIAquick PCR purification Kit (or other column-based purification system).
Wash twice during the purification process.
Store purified products at +4°C if not used immediately after amplification.
Store purified libraries at 4°C overnight for short-term storage or at -20°C freezer for extended storage up to 1 month before adapter ligation.
Determine concentration of each library using the QuBit Fluorometer.
Combine equal molar portions of each individual sample to prepare a pool for MiSeq run or HiSeq lane, ensuring the resulting amount is at least 300 ng.
Generate parallel libraries with similar content from samples of the same type and number of PCR cycles.
Mix obtained libraries in equal volume proportions to achieve homogeneous over-sequencing.
Ensure that libraries starting from different numbers of cells are mixed proportionally to maintain optimal UMI over-sequencing for comparative bioinformatic analysis.
Use pooled PCR products to prepare a sequencing library.
Apply the NEBNext Ultra DNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina according to manufacturer recommendations.
Alternatively, prepare separate libraries for each sample.
Use at least 300 ng of each PCR product.
Perform double-end sample barcoding in the second PCR amplification.
Ligate Illumina adapters separately to each library to protect from cross-sample contamination.
Pool libraries of interest with ligated Illumina adapters in equal volumes.
Purify target library using AMPure XP beads or agarose gel purification.
Prepare 2% agarose gel with 1x TBE buffer.
Run agarose gel electrophoresis at 120V for 60 minutes.
Excise the gel containing amplified libraries in the range of 600-750 nt.
Spike the library with 20% of PhiX library.
Analyze the resulting library using paired end Illumina MiSeq or HiSeq2500 sequencing.
Use standard Illumina sequencing primers for analysis.
